uncited: The scene is represented as a collection of $M$ 3D Gaussian points $GP$.
**Position** $X_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$: The center of the Gaussian.
**Projection**: Each 3D Gaussian $i$ is projected onto the 2D image plane.
**Sorting**: Gaussian points are sorted by depth for each tile on the image plane.
The core innovation of GS-W is the separation and fusion of appearance features.
**Feature Extraction**: Image features are extracted from a reference image using a U-Net model.
**Dynamic Feature Sampling**: For each Gaussian point $GP_i$, dynamic appearance features $d_{f}^i$ are sampled from the extracted feature maps using an **adaptive sampling strategy**.
**Fusion**: The intrinsic appearance feature $s_{f}^i$ (learnable per point) and the sampled dynamic appearance feature $d_{f}^i$ are fused with the position $X_i$ using a fusion network $M_f$.
**Loss Calculation**: The loss is computed between the rendered image $I_r$ and the ground truth reference image $I_{gt}$.
To mitigate the impact of transient occluders (e.g., moving people, vehicles), a **2D visibility map** $V_M \in \mathbb{R}^{1 \times H \times W}$ is employed.
This map is obtained from a U-Net model and facilitates segmentation between transient and static objects.
**Optimization**: All Gaussian attributes (position, covariance, opacity, intrinsic features $s_f^i$) are jointly optimized.
-   **Local Detail**: Global appearance representations (common in NeRF) struggle with high-frequency local changes.

-   **Memory**: Requires storage for intrinsic features per Gaussian point, increasing memory usage compared to standard 3DGS which typically uses a single SH coefficient set or simple color per point.
The exact memory overhead is not specified in the sources.
-   **Strengths**: Handles unconstrained image collections (wild data) with varying illumination, weather, and transient occluders.
-   **Limitations**: Requires a U-Net for feature extraction and visibility map generation, adding complexity to the training pipeline.
Performance depends on the quality of the SfM initialization and the visibility map accuracy.
-   **Origin**: Gaussian in the Wild (GS-W) was proposed to address the limitations of existing NeRF-based methods and standard 3DGS when applied to unconstrained image collections.
-   **Key Insight**: The appearance of a point in the real world is determined by its intrinsic material properties and dynamic environmental impacts.
